title: Nouns 6: Mixed Review (Naming the World)
description: Mixed review of the whole track. Read gender from the ending (with the soft-sign and male-person patches). Form the plural, with the seven-letter rule, the irregular -а / -я set, the truly irregular forms, and the plural-only / singular-only nouns. One system, the right form every time.
descriptionRussian: Итоговое повторение всего трека. Определи род по окончанию (с поправками на мягкий знак и значение). Образуй множественное число, помня о правиле семи букв, о наборе -а / -я, об исключениях и о словах только во множественном или только в единственном. Одна система — нужная форма каждый раз.
intro: Everything from the last five lessons arrives together here, mixed and unsorted, the way Russian actually hands words to you. Every noun comes down to the same two questions, asked in that order. What gender is it? And what is its plural? Get those two right and you can read or produce any A1 noun.
rules: Read gender from the ending: hard consonant → M; -а / -я → F; -о / -е → N. Then check the patches: soft sign -ь (memorise each), -а / -я male-person words are M (папа, дядя), and -мя words are N (время, имя).
The default plural is -ы (for hard M and feminine -а) or -и (for soft endings). The seven-letter rule overrides -ы with -и after Г, К, Х, Ж, Ш, Щ, Ч.
Neuter plurals are predictable: -о → -а, -е → -я (окно → окна, море → моря).

The irregular masculine -а / -я group is a memorised list: дом → дома, город → города, доктор → доктора, профессор → профессора, лес → леса, поезд → поезда, голос → голоса, глаз → глаза, паспорт → паспорта, цвет → цвета, учитель → учителя (with -я).

Truly irregular plurals and the no-singular / no-plural sets are small closed lists: друг → друзья, ребёнок → дети, мать → матери, имя → имена; часы / очки / деньги (no singular); молоко / любовь / счастье (no plural).
examples: книга → F (-а) → plural книги (seven-letter rule, after г).
ночь → F (soft-sign, memorised) → plural ночи (soft -ь → -и; ч also reinforces).
дом → M (hard consonant) → plural дома́ (irregular -а group, end-stressed).
ребёнок → M → plural дети (suppletive; a different word entirely).

rows.label: Irregular
cells: друг → друзья; ребёнок → дети; мать → матери

items.hint: Стол ends in a hard consonant, so it follows the regular default rule. Which ending do hard masculine nouns normally take in the plural?
items.explanation: Стол ends in a hard consonant and takes the default plural ending -ы: стол → столы. (The seven-letter rule does not apply, because -л is not one of the seven letters.)

items.hint: Soft-sign -ь nouns are memorised one by one, and дверь is one of the common feminine ones (like ночь, мать, дочь). So which gender?
items.explanation: Дверь is one of the high-frequency soft-sign feminines (alongside ночь, мать, дочь, тетрадь). The possessive must agree as feminine: моя дверь.

items.hint: The stem ends in ч, one of the seven letters (Г К Х Ж Ш Щ Ч). After those, Russian always writes -и and never -ы. So врач → ?
items.explanation: Врач ends in -ч, one of the seven letters. After ч, Russian writes -и, never -ы. Plural: врачи.

items.hint: This is a suppletive plural: a completely different word, just like ребёнок → дети. Which option is the everyday word for 'people'?
items.explanation: The plural of человек is a completely different word: люди (people), just as ребёнок becomes дети.

items.hint: Время ends in -я, which usually marks feminine, but it belongs to the small -мя group (имя, время), which is always the same gender. Which one?
items.explanation: Время is part of the closed -мя neuter set (with имя, племя, бремя, etc.). Despite the -я ending, agreement is always neuter: моё время, какое время?, времена прошли.

items.prompt: Which pair demonstrates the seven-letter rule?
items.promptEnglish: Which pair demonstrates the seven-letter rule?
items.hint: The rule fires only when the stem ends in Г, К, Х, Ж, Ш, Щ, Ч. Three options have plain hard or soft stems; one ends in г (look closely at книга).
items.explanation: Книга → книги fires the seven-letter rule: after г, -ы is forbidden, so -и takes over.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The plural of ребёнок is a completely different word: дети. The plural possessive is мои, and the plural past-tense verb is пришли.

minimalPairs.explanation: Друг has an irregular plural: друзья (with the stem change г → з and the -ья ending). The default -ы form (другы) does not exist in Russian.
Город is in the irregular masculine set: plural города́ (end-stressed). Городы does not exist in modern Russian.

patternRecognition.question: Which two rules combine to give ночи as the plural of ночь?
options: Suppletive: ночи is a different stem.
Soft -ь is replaced by -и; and the seven-letter rule applies (after ч).
patternRecognition.answer: Soft -ь is replaced by -и; and the seven-letter rule applies (after ч).
patternRecognition.explanation: Two rules reinforce each other. The soft sign -ь is replaced by -и in the plural. AND the stem ends in ч, one of the seven letters, so -ы would be impossible anyway. Either rule alone would give ночи; both apply here.

patternRecognition.question: Why is the plural of учитель the form учителя, not the expected учители?
options: Учитель is in the irregular -а / -я masculine plural group, with -я (because of the soft sign).
The soft sign -ь is just replaced by -и; учители is the plural.
patternRecognition.answer: Учитель is in the irregular -а / -я masculine plural group, with -я (because of the soft sign).
patternRecognition.explanation: Учитель belongs to the small irregular masculine set (with дом → дома, город → города, etc.) that takes stressed -а or -я in the plural. Because учитель ends in soft -ь, it takes -я rather than -а: учителя. The form учители is archaic and is not used in everyday Russian.

patternRecognition.question: What pattern gives имена as the plural of имя?
options: The -мя neuters insert -ен- before the plural ending.
The seven-letter rule fires after м.
patternRecognition.answer: The -мя neuters insert -ен- before the plural ending.
patternRecognition.explanation: The -мя neuters (имя, время, племя, etc.) form their plural by inserting a syllable -ен- before the ending: имя → имена, время → времена. М is not one of the seven letters, so the spelling rule does not apply.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each noun by gender. Watch for the soft-sign, male-person, and -мя patches from lesson 2.

reviewVocab.definition: Two questions. (1) Gender: read the ending, then patches (-ь memorise, male-person -а / -я is M, -мя is N). (2) Plural: default -ы / -и, seven-letter override, irregular masculine, truly irregular, or no plural at all.
reviewVocab.example: Книга: F (-а) → книги (seven-letter). Учитель: M (-тель) → учителя́. Время: N (-мя) → времена.

reviewVocab.definition: After Г, К, Х, Ж, Ш, Щ, Ч, Russian never writes -ы; always -и. The rule applies in plurals and far beyond.
reviewVocab.example: Книга → книги. Ученик → ученики. Врач → врачи. Нож → ножи.

reviewVocab.definition: plural-only nouns (часы, очки, ножницы, деньги, брюки, джинсы) have no singular; use одни for 'one'. Singular-only nouns (молоко, мясо, сахар, хлеб, соль, любовь, счастье, дружба, мебель) have no plural in normal Russian.
reviewVocab.example: Одни часы. Я люблю молоко. В комнате новая мебель.
